title: Recursion in three rounds
description: Round 1: draw the calls that wait in a linear recursion. Round 2: recurse on a shrinking window and on nested containers. Round 3: trace a branching recurrence, compute each state once, measure both, and count plans for inputs too deep to recurse on.

learned: Tell a recursive definition from the process it generates, and draw the calls that are waiting.
Argue termination from an input that shrinks toward a base case, separately from correctness.
See repeated work in a branching recursion and compute each state once.
Pick an order of evaluation that needs no deep chain of waiting calls.
recap.invariant: Every stored answer is correct for its state, and it is stored only after the answers it depends on are complete.
recap.complexity: Counting one step per state expansion or addition, and leaving drawing out: the naive route count expands exponentially many states in n, the memoized one expands n, and ordered packing needs at most n times the number of sizes additions. Waiting calls are counted separately: the memoized recursion is still n deep.
recap.common_mistake: Assuming that memoization or a call in tail position removes Python's call depth.
in_real_programs: CPython enforces a recursion limit (1,000 by default) and does not optimize tail calls.

retrieval.question: Module 2: why can separate calls use the same parameter name independently?
retrieval.answer: Each call has its own frame with its own binding for the parameter; the same spelling does not mean the same binding.
